title: Elodie and the Bakery
premise: Jonah Thackeray, a pastry chef whose café is three missed payments from collapse, hires Elodie Marsh—a sharp-eyed event planner he barely knows—to pose as his girlfriend at a family reunion where his estranged, powerful uncle will decide whether to forgive a debt that could save the bakery. What begins as a transaction deepens into something real, but Elodie discovers the debt was manufactured by the uncle to seize the café's riverside property for a development scheme. Choosing justice over safety, Jonah and Elodie expose the scheme at a public gala, costing Jonah the family money but winning back the bakery through the community his pastries fed for years—and winning each other in the process.
about_author: Sebastian Nystrom is a former line cook who traded kitchen shifts for quiet mornings and long manuscripts, writing love stories set in places where people work with their hands. He lives in a small coastal town where he is known, reliably, for showing up at every bakery within cycling distance.

chapters.title: Three Payments from Gone
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Facing a final notice and his uncle's ultimatum, Jonah invents a girlfriend on the spot when his mother calls. The beat is desperation masked as control—he treats his heart like a muscle he can train into stillness.

chapters.title: The Girl at Table Nine
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie, an event planner who notices everything, has watched Jonah for months from her corner table. When he blurts out his absurd proposal, she surprises them both by negotiating terms. Beat: two guarded people finding an unexpected bargain.

chapters.title: Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Over stolen evenings in the closed bakery, they build a fake history—first date, first fight, first kiss—and the practice kisses stop feeling like practice. Beat: intimacy creeping past the contract's fine print.

chapters.title: The Reunion
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. At the lakeside reunion, Elodie plays her role flawlessly and charms even Uncle Ambrose—but Jonah realizes he's watching her, not performing. Beat: the fake date feeling too real by dessert, just as the blurb promises.

chapters.title: Ambrose's Offer
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Ambrose privately offers to forgive the debt if Jonah sells the building, revealing a predatory gleam Elodie recognizes from corporate events she's staged. Beat: the romance plot and the power plot colliding.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Says
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Elodie digs into the café's finances and finds the missed payments trace to a loan Jonah never took—Ambrose manufactured the default. Beat: the turn from romance to justice; Elodie must decide whether to tell Jonah.

chapters.title: The Truth at Closing Time
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Elodie shows him the ledger; his relief at the café's innocence curdles into rage at his family—and fear that Elodie stayed only for the cause. Beat: the relationship's lowest point, honesty demanded at last.

chapters.title: Gala Night
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At Ambrose's development gala, Jonah and Elodie go public with the forged loan, backed by a supplier's records and a room full of townsfolk the bakery fed for a decade. Beat: the climax—justice outside the law, at maximum cost.

chapters.title: Ash and Sugar
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Disowned but vindicated, Jonah reopens the bakery to a line out the door; Ambrose's scheme collapses under investigation. Yet Elodie, her contract long expired, is packing to leave. Beat: victory hollowed by her absence.

chapters.title: Elodie and the Bakery
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Jonah finds her at the train platform and, for the first time, asks for something instead of offering terms. She stays—not for a contract, but because he finally let himself be seen. Beat: the heart, untrained at last, choosing freely.
